### Where were you using Orca?

Not applicable

### Orca version

### Details

OpenCode’s legacy MessageV2 JSON format stores message metadata under storage/message/<sessionId> and content under storage/part/<messageId>. **Reproduction:**

1. Create a legacy session JSON file under storage/session/<project>/ses_saved.json.
2. Put a user message and an assistant message under storage/message/ses_saved, with their id, role and time metadata but no content field.
3. Put their text/reasoning/tool records under storage/part/<messageId>/<partId>.json. Write the two user text files in reverse directory order to exercise recorded part ordering; include an older inline message as a control.
4. Call parseOpenCodeSessionFile with a transcript consumer. Inspect firstUserPrompt, previewMessages and emitted transcript content.
5. Open previous-version parse/search SQLite stores containing those unchanged JSON files. Verify that the upgrade schedules only the affected JSON records for rereading.

Regression fixtures on the proposed branch:

- https://github.com/Afloat16/orca/blob/afloat16/orca50-20261127-opencode-json-message-parts/src/main/ai-vault/scanners/opencode/session-scanner-opencode-json-parts.test.ts

**Expected behavior:** The prompt is “Inspect the build failure.\nKeep the command output.” Replies, reasoning, tool calls/results and the inline control are emitted. Only affected JSON cache rows/cursors are invalidated once; SQLite-backed sessions and other agents remain intact.

Locally exercised on Linux with Node 24.22.3.

### Details

git for-each-ref emits worktreepath literally. The history catalog split the output on every newline even though a pathname can contain a newline on POSIX filesystems. That truncates the path used to match a Git Graph ref to a registered workspace.

**Reproduction:**

1. On a POSIX filesystem, create a temporary Git repository and an initial commit.
2. Add a linked worktree on feature at a path whose final component is review followed by a literal newline and workspace.

**Observed before:** The feature ref retains only the path through “review”; the rest of the pathname is split into a bogus record. Git Graph cannot match the complete registered workspace path.

**Expected behavior:** The feature ref retains the complete “review\nworkspace” path. The main ref still reports its ordinary repository path.

**Validation:** One real-Git regression passes on Linux. The same fixture failed against the original catalog parser because the linked worktree path was truncated. draft.issueTitle: [Bug]: Creating a review strips literal branch prefixes from explicitly qualified base refs
draft.issueBody:
### Where were you using Orca?

Other — source-level reproduction of the affected production operation

### Operating system

Linux

### Remote host operating system

Not applicable

### Orca version

Source checkout at 9890ea181c0f9ae59fb82da64c4a6fbc0504a817

### Details

A full ref such as refs/heads/origin/topic names a branch literally called origin/topic. The shared normalizer removed the namespace and then stripped origin/ again. Main-process creation preflight also normalized an already-normalized base a second time. A valid published base is rejected as topic, or the request can target topic when that separate branch exists.

**Reproduction:**

1. Create a real repository with a clean, published feature branch, an ordinary origin/main tracking ref, and a branch origin/topic with tracking ref refs/remotes/origin/origin/topic.
2. Call createHostedReview for feature with base = refs/heads/origin/topic. The public hostedReview.create RPC accepts and forwards this explicit base string.
3. Repeat with base = refs/remotes/origin/origin/topic.
4. Use base = origin/main as an ordinary control. In a local protocol fixture, inspect the final provider POST body without creating a live remote review.

Regression fixtures on the proposed branch:

- https://github.com/Afloat16/orca/blob/afloat16/orca50-20261127-hosted-review-qualified-base/src/shared/source-control/hosted-review/hosted-review-qualified-base.test.ts

**Observed before:** Both explicit full refs are rejected as base_not_on_remote with the incorrect base “topic”. The ordinary origin/main control succeeds.

**Expected behavior:** Both explicit forms pass preflight and send base “origin/topic” to the provider. The ordinary origin/main control still sends “main”.

**Validation:** The focused parser regression failed against the exact original helper: expected origin/topic, received topic; it passes after the fix. A separate validation-only probe calls the actual createHostedReview entry point with a real temporary Git repository and replaces only external HTTP responses. That probe failed before the fix and now confirms both explicit forms reach Gitea with base origin/topic, while origin/main still submits main. The full-create probe is not added to the unit suite because it validates wiring rather than a separate parser invariant.

Locally exercised on Linux with Node 24.22.3. Provider requests in the qualified-reference reproduction use an external HTTP fixture; no live remote review is created by the probe.

Primary references:

- https://git-scm.com/docs/git-check-ref-format
draft.prTemplate:
## ELI5

Keep the branch name the caller explicitly selected when creating a pull request or merge request.

## What Changed

- Remove at most one explicit Git ref namespace and preserve the literal branch name that remains.
- Keep the original submitted base when invoking creation eligibility, so the remote-ref check does not reinterpret a shortened branch name.
- Preserve established short origin/main and upstream/main handling; all five supported creation providers continue using the shared normalizer.

## Why

A full ref such as refs/heads/origin/topic names a branch literally called origin/topic. The shared normalizer removed the namespace and then stripped origin/ again. Main-process creation preflight also normalized an already-normalized base a second time. A valid published base is rejected as topic, or the request can target topic when that separate branch exists.

## Linked Issue

Fixes #ISSUE_NUMBER

## Visual Proof

N/A

No graphical layout or interaction component changes. The following before/after results come from the affected production operation with the same fixture input.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Both explicit full refs are rejected as base_not_on_remote with the incorrect base “topic”. The ordinary origin/main control succeeds. | Both explicit forms pass preflight and send base “origin/topic” to the provider. The ordinary origin/main control still sends “main”. |

## Testing

- [x] I manually tested these changes locally through the production-entry reproductions described below
- [x] Automated tests added/updated, or explained why not below
- [x] Every added test fails without this change and avoids the test anti-patterns

Git reference parsing and branch-identity integrity. One compact committed parser case covers explicit namespaces and ordinary short-ref controls.

The focused parser regression failed against the exact original helper: expected origin/topic, received topic; it passes after the fix. A separate validation-only probe calls the actual createHostedReview entry point with a real temporary Git repository and replaces only external HTTP responses. That probe failed before the fix and now confirms both explicit forms reach Gitea with base origin/topic, while origin/main still submits main. The full-create probe is not added to the unit suite because it validates wiring rather than a separate parser invariant.

Reproduce the focused tests with:

```sh
pnpm test src/shared/source-control/hosted-review/hosted-review-qualified-base.test.ts --maxWorkers=2
```

Locally executed through the repository’s test-runtime runner on Linux with Node 24.22.3. macOS, Windows and remote SSH execution are not claimed.

Final integrated validation: 32 focused regression tests in 22 files passed, including the unchanged archive-write failure case that had timed out under earlier heavy concurrent checking. The Drive performance contract passed separately (1 file/1 test). Changed-code quality passed with zero new findings across 129 changed paths; final touched-file formatting and git diff --check passed. Node typechecking passed for 17,026 files and web typechecking for 16,094 files using the repository-supported Bun compiler with one worker. These are aggregate validation results for the prepared contributions, not per-PR test counts.

The required `pnpm check:changed --base=9890ea181c0f9ae59fb82da64c4a6fbc0504a817` was attempted after the final edits. Its workspace-package build is blocked because this environment rejects the tsx CLI local IPC socket (`listen EPERM`). The default tsrs typechecker was also terminated with SIGKILL; the supported Bun typechecking route completed successfully. The complete gate/build is not claimed to pass and still requires CI.

## Performance

None, because the fix changes only existing string normalization and passes the original input through preflight. It adds no Git calls, API calls, polling or allocations proportional to repository size.

## Risk

**Level:** Low

The ambiguous bare string origin/topic keeps its established short-ref interpretation; this fix preserves the information carried by explicit full refs. The shared helper affects GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps and Gitea, so ordinary remote prefixes remain covered. A plain revert restores the previous behavior; no persisted schema or source refs are changed.

## AI Disclosure

Core contribution owner: @Afloat16. Required tooling disclosure: GPT-6 Astra Pro was used for implementation and review.

## Review

Reviewed the public RPC input, main preflight, remote-ref existence check and final provider request. The fix is provider-neutral and platform-neutral, and retains existing local/SSH execution routing. It adds no shell command or permission change and leaves mobile wire fields intact. The main creation change is one input-preservation line; there is no graphical layout change.

## Agent skill upstream boundary

- [x] Not applicable: this change copies or mechanically translates no upstream skill-installer source, tests, fixtures, registry entries, path tables, comments or documentation.

## Notes

Git documents refs/heads as the branch namespace and permits slash-separated branch components. Related compare-base and older-client label fixes (#5127, #18220 and #43448) do not repair hosted review creation. The unavailable-lookup work in #11678 is also distinct.
